title: Arrays versus slices: what is actually passed around

videos.script: Lesson 10 was about values of one type meeting another. This lesson is about holding many values at once. Go has two ways to do it, and they look almost the same on the screen. {{array}} An array has a fixed length, and the length is part of its type. Copy one and you get a second array, every element of it. {{slice}} A slice is different. It holds no elements of its own. It is a small window onto an array, three numbers wide: where it starts, how many elements it shows, and how far it could reach. {{share}} Two slices can look at the same array. Change an element through one, and the other sees it. {{function}} That is what decides what a function receives. Hand it an array and it works on a copy. Hand it a slice and it can change your elements, but it cannot make your slice longer. By the end you will know which one you are passing, and why the answer matters.
